title: Fourier weight bound for indicators
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$. Write $\alpha=\mathbb E[f]$, and assume $\alpha>0$, $k>0$, and $k\le2\log(1/\alpha)$. Then the Fourier weight on levels at most $k$ satisfies $\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2\le\left(\frac{2e}{k}\log(1/\alpha)\right)^k\alpha^2$, with Fourier coefficients and expectation under the uniform measure.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$k\le2\log(1/\mathbb E[f])$ when written as $2\log(1/\alpha)$ with $\alpha=\mathbb E[f]$
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ have uniform mean $\alpha>0$, and let $k$ be a positive integer with $k\le2\log(1/\alpha)$. Then $\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2\le((2e/k)\log(1/\alpha))^k\alpha^2$.
